drivers.label: New-chip compute rent, spot ($/W-yr of nameplate)
drivers.source: src 24 (Google Cloud Services Agreement FWP: $920M/month from Oct-2026, ~110,000 GPUs); src 25 (Q3 call, CFO Bret Johnsen: 'Pricing is currently tracking slightly above the high end of the $30 to $50 per watt range'; CEO Elon Musk: short-term contracts renewing at higher dollars per watt); src 6 (SemiAnalysis 2026-08-07: large-scale near-term compute 'priced at a huge premium - up to $50B/GW/year'); src 7 (Uvik GPU price index, prices captured 2026-10-07: B300 on-demand median $9.50/GPU-hr; 'Prices are rising in 2026' (after falling in 2025); H100 readings near $2.8 (SemiAnalysis H100 composite $2.82 in Apr-26; Silicon Data $2.81 and Ornn $2.86 in Oct, different indices, not a like-for-like series); single-provider rises in October: Nebius H100 on-demand $3.85 -> $4.50 on 1 Oct, AWS Capacity Blocks ~+15% with on-demand unchanged); src 8 (Introl: H100 rental $8 -> $2.85-3.50, '64% from peak levels in late 2024', no time span; Silicon Data H100 index -23% Sep-2024 to Jun-2025); src 18 (S&P Global: ~$1.3T 2027 capex at six hyperscalers); src 62 (Goldman Sachs via TrendForce 2026-10-16: CoWoS 1.275M wafers 2026, 2.73M 2027, 3.48M 2028); src 19 (CTEE rack power, for the $/W conversion)
drivers.derivation: Actual quarters are not a SpaceX disclosure and enter no value (reported quarters book filed revenue; the SOTP flows start at the horizon): 2025 $42 is a placeholder, Q1-Q3 2026 $50 (the $30-50 range discussed on the Q2 call, where Musk's guess was 'somewhere between $30 and $50'; the Q3 CFO: 'slightly above the high end of the $30 to $50 per watt range we were discussing just last quarter'). Q4-26 $51.62, built from the one filed price for capacity that starts in the quarter: the Google Cloud Services Agreement, $920M a month from October 2026 for ~110,000 GPUs (src 24), is $11,040M a year over ~214 MW at 1.944 kW per GPU (GB300 NVL72 140 kW / 72, src 19) = $51.62/W-yr. It sits where the CFO (Bret Johnsen) put current pricing on the Q3 call, 'slightly above the high end of the $30 to $50 per watt range' (src 25), and with the CEO's (Elon Musk) word that contracts renew 'at higher dollars per watt' (src 25) and SemiAnalysis' 'up to $50B/GW/year' for near-term large-scale compute (src 6). The Google rate was agreed in June 2026, before the 2026 rise in new-chip rent (Uvik 'prices are rising in 2026', src 7; Morgan Stanley B300 1-year index up >50% YTD to Sep-26, src 13), so as a Q4 spot level it leans conservative. The Anthropic contract is an older long-dated price, not a Q4 spot reading: ~$23.7/W-yr is our conversion ($1.25B a month = $15.0B a year over ~325,000 GPUs x 1.944 kW = ~632 MW; the 424B4, src 2, files the fee and the GPU count, no per-watt price). Carry trace 2026-11-18 replaced the earlier $52, a hand step off the Q3 level with no build of its own. 2027: $52 / $51 / $49 / $47: the shortage holds into mid-2027 on management's word (renewals at higher $/W, src 25) and October price rises at single providers (Nebius, AWS capacity blocks, src 7); by chip generation, new-chip rent is still rising (Morgan Stanley: Compute Desk B300 1-year rental index up >50% YTD to Sep-26, src 13; Uvik: 'prices are rising in 2026', src 7) while H100 readings sit near $2.8. The fade from mid-2027 rests on its own case, not on a flat index: B300/GB300 volume ramped in 2026, and on the H100 precedent on-demand rent fell from $8 to $2.85-3.50 an hour, '64% from peak levels in late 2024', as production caught up with shortage-era orders, while the Silicon Data H100 index fell 23% in under a year ($3.06 Sep-2024 to $2.36 Jun-2025) (Introl, src 8); in 2027 Vera Rubin is in full production (src 36) with TSMC CoWoS capacity +114% to 2.73M wafers (Goldman Sachs via TrendForce 2026-10-16, src 62; it replaces the April KeyBanc +29%, src 33, now stale) and ~$1.3T of hyperscaler capex (src 18), so the newest-chip premium erodes from mid-2027. 2028: $45 / $43 / $41 / $39: through today's newest-chip index level, ~$43/W-yr (our conversion: Uvik B300 median $9.50/GPU-hr x 8,760 h / 1.94 kW per GPU, GB300 NVL72 140 kW / 72, src 7, 19), to ~10% below it by Q4-28 as the supply wave lands, the way H100 on-demand rent fell 64% from its late-2024 peak as production caught up with shortage-era orders (src 8; no time span given). After FY2028 (SOTP only): $36-30 (2029), $29-25 (2030), $23.5 (2031) and the $20.04 NPV-0 price from 2032 (at 90% utilization) (a competitive new build earns its cost of capital). The ~$42-44/W-yr figures are our conversions of hourly GPU prices, not published $/W-yr. Other evidence-based builds (judgment_alternatives): hold into 2029, collapse in 2027-28, flat at today's ~$43 index level, the signed contracts at their filed rates, MS revenue per watt (Kilian kept the booked fade on 2026-11-16; decided_alternatives).
